kurz: Cook butter and flour in equal parts, then stir in liquid bit by bit. The base for béchamel and many pale sauces.
bild_im_kopf: Like wrapping flour in fat beforehand: every grain is surrounded by fat and cannot stick to its neighbours.
was_passiert: The fat coats the flour grains and keeps them apart. When liquid is added, they swell one by one instead of forming lumps. The longer the roux toasts, the nuttier it tastes, but the less it thickens.
faustregeln: Dark roux: more flavour, less thickening.
50 g butter and 50 g flour thicken about a litre of milk into a medium béchamel (as a guide).
schritte: Melt butter and stir in the same weight of flour (e.g. 50 g and 50 g).
Cook for 2–3 minutes while stirring, longer for dark sauces.
Stir in the liquid bit by bit, not the other way round.
Bring to the boil and simmer gently for a few minutes until there is no floury taste left.
